test.llm_feedback:
Your approach of decomposing the motion into radial and angular components is the right idea, but the key step—expressing \(\dot\theta\)—needs more care. In your solution you treated \(\dot\theta=v\cos(\pi/N)\) as a constant, but in fact the angular speed depends on the current radius \(r\). One finds by geometry that 
\[
\dot r=-v\sin\bigl(\pi/N\bigr), 
\qquad 
r\,\dot\theta=v\cos\bigl(\pi/N\bigr),
\]
so 
\[
\frac{dr}{d\theta}=\frac{\dot r}{\dot\theta}
=-\tan\bigl(\pi/N\bigr)\,r\,,
\]
not a constant. Solving this separable ODE gives the familiar logarithmic spiral
\[
r(\theta)=R\exp\!\bigl(-\theta\cot(\pi/N)\bigr).
\]
To improve, please (1) re-derive the angular velocity including its \(1/r\) factor, (2) set up and solve the separable ODE carefully, and (3) check your integration constant by enforcing \(r(0)=R\). This will yield the correct exponential form rather than a linear relation.
